projects.title: RAG-Based Intelligent Q&A System for Postgraduate Entrance Exam Knowledge
projects.summary:
Background: integrated a computer science postgraduate entrance exam knowledge base (official textbooks, past papers, etc.) with LLM and RAG technology to build a locally deployable intelligent Q&A system for students, improving the efficiency and accuracy of LLM retrieval of key knowledge while reducing hallucinations and helping exam candidates review efficiently.
Offline indexing: used the Qwen3-Embedding-8b model with multi-representation and other representation techniques to vectorize the cleaned data, built an efficient hierarchical vector index and stored it distributed in the ChromaDB vector database.
Question handling: based on conversation history, used Qwen3-8b deployed locally with Ollama for context compression and semantic understanding, turning ambiguous natural-language queries into structured instructions through question rewriting and logical analysis.
Retrieval: used Adaptive-RAG for subject-aware logical routing and dynamic scheduling of retrieval strategies, combining BM25 (keyword matching) and vector retrieval (semantic similarity) for hybrid retrieval to suit questions from different subjects.
Post-retrieval processing: built a multi-round retrieval strategy based on Self-RAG and optimized ranking with two rounds of post-processing: first fusing and deduplicating multi-source heterogeneous results with the RRF algorithm, then calling a Cohere model for semantics-aware fine-grained reranking to ensure the accuracy of the RAG context.
Generation: used prompt templates and the LLM's CoT reasoning to guide the model to produce clearly structured, logically rigorous professional answers, with a citation mechanism so key details of answers can be traced and verified against retrieval sources.
Results: in end-to-end evaluation on a self-built sample set, key-information answer accuracy rose from 74% to 92% compared with LLM answers without RAG.

projects.title: Campus Service Intelligent Assistant (in testing and development)
projects.summary:
Developed an intelligent Agent for students on campus that combines free-classroom lookup, class auditing assistant, canteen dish recommendations, flea market and other campus life services, addressing the inefficiency of repeated verification and manual lookup across separate services; in testing it has cut service time by 40% and supports personalized features.
Memory architecture: designed a 'short-term cache + long-term vector retrieval' memory architecture that uses student conversations and service data to automatically extract student profiles and key queries, with periodic refresh and personalized answer configuration (e.g. frequently used classrooms, library seat booking).
Modular MCP servers: wrapped tools such as classroom lookup and dish recommendation and split them by service type into query, recommendation and review MCP servers, with Agent scheduling for automatic tool routing, supporting quick extension with new services (e.g. library borrowing, campus shuttle lookup).
Multimodal interaction: integrated the Doubao multimodal model to support voice queries and spoken results (convenient on the move) and image feedback (e.g. a map of free classrooms to help students choose), strengthening interaction in voice and visual scenarios.
Planning and reasoning: implemented intent recognition based on GPT-4o and combined ReAct, CoT and self-consistency strategies for multi-turn reasoning and action planning, significantly improving task execution accuracy and logical consistency.
